evidence_frontier.status: Alpha5 remains active. Exp021 identified a 4,278‑parameter w8 compression candidate that was 10 fewer Q.ANT correct predictions out of 1000 than the Alpha5 control. The preregistered integer‑count gate retained Alpha5. The next preregistered question is to test reproducibility of the w8 boundary with a fresh seed set.

analysis: Observations: (1) Redundant three‑head readout improves logit MAE and does not hurt aggregate Q.ANT correct counts (Exp020). (2) Alpha5 uses a fixed local window width of 16 dimensions. (3) No experiment has varied the local representation width while keeping the redundant readout. (4) Exp021 showed a compression candidate (w8) can lose up to 10 correct predictions, establishing a relative‑performance gate of "candidate_correct ≥ control_correct − 10" for confirmation. Hypothesis: Decreasing the local window width below 16 (e.g., to 12 or 8) will reduce parameter count while preserving the redundant readout’s robustness, yielding aggregate Q.ANT correct counts within 10 of the Alpha5 control on a fresh seed set and maintaining or improving logit MAE.
hypothesis: Narrower local representations (width < 16) combined with the three‑head averaged readout will keep aggregate Q.ANT correct predictions within the 10‑prediction tolerance of the Alpha5 control and will lower total parameter count, potentially further reducing logit MAE.

proposal.title: Local‑Width Compression with Redundant Readout on ECG200
proposal.research_question: Can reducing the per‑window representation width below 16 dimensions preserve the promoted redundant readout’s accuracy and logit agreement while decreasing model size?
proposal.rationale: Alpha5’s promotion demonstrated that redundant readout yields numerical‑agreement benefits. Model size is still dominated by the 16‑dimensional local windows. Prior compression (w8) lost exactly 10 correct predictions, establishing a clear relative‑performance gate. Testing narrower widths will reveal whether the readout redundancy compensates for reduced local capacity, enabling a smaller yet equally robust architecture.

procedure: Generate a fresh preregistered set of N=5 random seeds distinct from those used in Exp020 and Exp021.
For each seed, train Alpha5 (control) with its original local_width = 16 and three‑head readout for a fixed number of epochs (max_epochs).

For each candidate width, instantiate the same architecture but replace the 16‑dimensional local window projection with the specified local_width while keeping all other layers and the three‑head readout unchanged.
Evaluate on the ECG200 test set (100 samples) and record aggregate Q.ANT correct predictions and mean absolute logit error for each seed.
Compute per‑candidate totals across seeds (aggregate_correct = sum over seeds of correct predictions).
Apply the confirmation gate: candidate_correct ≥ control_correct − 10 and candidate_logit_MAE ≤ control_logit_MAE.

success_criteria.aggregate_correct_gate: candidate_correct ≥ control_correct − 10 on the combined 5 × 100 test predictions

proposal.risks: Potential over‑compression leading to >10‑prediction drop; variance across seeds may obscure small differences; software‑simulation may not capture hardware‑level effects; limited seed count may reduce statistical power.
